rationale: design-import-refactor: generic change landed in Pulp per owner decision 2026-10-04; Vellum inherits (see inheritance ledger); SkiaSurface (skia_surface.cpp) now sizes from the swapchain where a presentable surface has one: read_current_rgba() reads back at the size of the surface it drew into, and the persistent-scene target takes the swapchain's size instead of logical width x scale. The two are equal unless a host sizes the swapchain from the platform's physical client rect, which at a fractional scale is a pixel larger (1001 px at 1.5x against 667 x 1.5 = 1000); the readback then cropped the frame and the scene left the drawable's last column unpainted. No frame, present, readback-format, design-import, Chromium, packaging or authority boundary moves; the Pulp render target has not adopted a Vellum package.
tests: ctest --test-dir build -R 'SkiaSurface persistent scene matches a fractional-DPI swapchain'
ctest --test-dir build -R 'SkiaSurface reads back a presentable frame at the swapchain'
